paper_metadata.title: Composition effect on the elastic properties of model NiCo-based superalloys

density functional theory (DFT) calculations were conducted by using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP), a projector augmented wave method, and the generalised gradient approximation (GGA) in the parameterisation introduced by Perdew, Burke, Ernzerhop (PBE). The minimum cut-off of the plane wave energy is 350 eV. The spacing between k-points is 0.18 Å-1.
For the selected (B) systems, a four-atom lattice was constructed for the calculation of elastic constants.
By employing the ATAT package, the SQSs were generated with shape restrictions over the entire concentration range for L12 cells containing 64 atoms of (C), and (D) systems.

Here, we selected the possible systems in NiCo-based superalloys, including: (A) NiCo solution (γ phase) both in the paramagnetic state and ferromagnetic state.
(B) binary L12 systems (γ′ phase), including Co3Al, Ni3Al, Co3W, Ni3W, Co3Ti, and Ni3Ti.
(C) ternary L12 systems (γ′ phase), including (Ni,Co)3Al, Co3(Al,W), Ni3(Al,W), Co3(Al,Ti), and Ni3(Al,Ti)
(D) quaternary L12 systems (γ′ phase), including (Ni,Co)3(Al,W), and (Ni,Co)3(Al,Ti).
To obtain the total energies and extract the elastic constants of the supercells, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were conducted by using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP)
For the selected (B) systems, a four-atom lattice was constructed for the calculation of elastic constants.
By employing the ATAT package, the SQSs were generated with shape restrictions over the entire concentration range for L12 cells containing 64 atoms of (C), and (D) systems.
